transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE); Marcus Chen (Redwood SE); Raj Patel (CTO, Neptune); Maya Singh (ML Engineer); Liam O'Connor (SecOps); Priya Rao (Product)

Auto-summary: quick discovery on model choice, very long context, multilingual coverage, and tool-calling. Agreed next steps for SE benchmark and docs.

00:00 Elena: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, do you all see my screen?
00:04 Raj: Yep, looks good. Thanks Elena.
00:07 Elena: quick intro: i'm Elena, AE at Redwood, with Marcus our solutions engineer. we usually do a short discovery to understand workload — latency, cost targets, context length — and then propose hosted vs dedicated vs private.
00:20 Marcus: hi, quick nod. we want to make sure the model selection aligns with your eval metrics — multilingual, tool-calling, and those very long documents you mentioned in the RFP.
00:34 Priya: yes thanks. high level — Neptune builds summarization and Q&A over enterprise docs plus a customer-facing assistant. we hit roughly 40 to 60k token sequences in some workflows (legal documents + long transcripts).
00:48 Maya: we also need Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese support; about 12 languages in total.
00:53 Liam: security wise we need VPC, KMS, SSO integrations and an on-prem option if data residency or regulator requires it.
01:02 Marcus: good, that's super helpful. on the long-context question: we have a couple of strategies — use models with native 64k+ context, or use chunking with a retrieval/recache pattern and KV cache. each has tradeoffs in latency and cost.
01:18 Raj: can you explain more on the KV cache? i've seen notes but not sure on real impact.
01:24 Marcus: yeah so KV cache is basically the key-value cache for transformer past states. when you do streaming or multi-turns you can avoid recomputing earlier tokens. we do prefix caching and also offer automatic prefix reuse. in practice for 50k tokens you'll see different memory & latency profiles depending on quantization and model architecture.
01:40 Maya: do you support tool-calling / function calls? we need to run code tools and external APIs from the assistant.
01:45 Elena: yes — Redwood supports function-calling patterns in the API and structured output; for Dedicated/Private we can enable direct network egress rules so tool calls can hit internal services. for Hosted we proxy or you can route through your own VPC connectors.
01:58 Raj: model choices — are we looking at open models only? we want to avoid closed LLM licensing costs but need strong instruction following and multilingual accuracy.
02:07 Marcus: typically we'd benchmark multiple open weights. for multilingual and long-context we often try a few variants: 1) a 70B-ish open model with 64k context (ModelA-64k), 2) a quantized 1.4B-2.7B family with retrieval and heavy caching (ModelLite + retriever), and 3) some hybrid (ModelX tuned). each will have different latency/cost.
02:25 Maya: what's the latency we'd expect for 50k context end-to-end?
02:29 Marcus: depends. if you stream and reuse KV cache after initial build, tail latencies per request might be in the low hundreds of ms for incremental additions; initial full-context encodes are heavier. with Dedicated GPUs and optimized kernels we can hit single-digit token ms in many cases but the total end-to-end also depends on retrieval and post-processing.
02:46 Liam: if we go Dedicated, are we guaranteed single-tenant physical GPUs or shared?
02:50 Elena: Dedicated is reserved capacity — your fleet is isolated logically and we can provide tenant isolation guarantees; there are options for predictable throughput and burst policies. for strict regulatory needs we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem).
03:03 Raj: what's the difference on cost structure between Hosted and Dedicated?
03:07 Elena: Hosted is usage-based (per-token), easy to start. Dedicated is committed capacity (monthly/annual) — better unit economics at scale and predictable latency. Private has platform fee plus support and possibly infra cost. We'll send a side-by-side example.
03:19 Maya: we care about quantization — does Redwood support 4-bit quantization and do you manage model distros?
03:25 Marcus: yes we support quantized runtimes and have quantization profiles; kernel selection and compilation target will be used to pick the best backend. quantization reduces memory and cost but may impact generation quality for instruction-heavy multilingual cases, so we recommend A/B comparing a few quant levels.
03:40 Raj: we noticed some vendors lose hallucination control after quantization. is Redwood doing evals tied to prompt sets?
03:45 Marcus: absolutely — we tie quality monitoring to prompt sets and can run evals during pilot; Redwood Optimize gives regression alerts if quality drops after a quant or model swap.
03:56 Priya: on the topic of tool-calling, latency matters because some calls will do a function call, then you call our internal API, then continue. can Redwood support synchronous internal tool calls without going over public internet?
04:09 Elena: for Dedicated we can set up VPC peering or Private we can deploy the runtime inside your network so tool-calls are local; Hosted can be proxied via connector. Security team will need docs for allowed egress.
04:20 Liam: can you share SOC2 and KMS integration docs now?
04:23 Elena: sure — i'll include SOC2 report, KMS/HSM integration guide, and our security whitepaper in the follow-up.
04:29 Raj: for multilingual accuracy, do you have tokenization differences? we used a tokenizer that undercounts for Japanese which affects prompt length.
04:36 Marcus: tokenization varies by model; part of the benchmark will measure tokenization overhead and effective context in characters. we'll include per-language tokenization stats.
04:46 Maya: is there an off-the-shelf approach for 50k context? we tried chunking with retrieval but the coherence drops.
04:52 Marcus: for coherence, models with native long context are best. 64k context models keep the entire context in memory so you get continuity. our runtime supports optimized attention kernels which help with performance. but those models are bigger and cost more per token.
05:06 Raj: curious about fallback policies — if Dedicated capacity saturates do you spill to Hosted?
05:11 Elena: yes we can define routing policies: prefer Dedicated, fallback to Hosted with a compatible model variant or lower context. we can also do canary rollouts and A/B.
05:21 Priya: do you have SDKs for our stack? we use Node + Python microservices.
05:25 Elena: yes SDKs for both and example repo. we'll include quickstart.
05:29 Maya: can you run a perf bench where we push 10 concurrent sessions with 50k contexts and measure throughput and latency and provide token-cost estimates?
05:36 Marcus: yes we can run that. for reproducibility please give a representative prompt set and any constraints on beam/temperature.
05:42 Maya: will do — i'll share prompts after this call.
05:45 Raj: what's the usual pilot length?
05:47 Elena: typical pilots are 4–12 weeks depending on benchmarks; given you need long-context perf and multilingual evals i'd suggest 6 weeks with an initial week for setup, 3 weeks of benching/evals, then 2 weeks of iteration.
06:00 Liam: and auditing? we need full request logs, redaction guidance, and audit export.
06:05 Marcus: we provide per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and audit logs with retention configs. for Private deployments logs can be kept entirely on-prem.
06:15 Priya: do you support model pinning and rollbacks?
06:18 Marcus: yes rollouts and automatic rollback policies; you can pin model versions at route-level.
06:23 Raj: about data residency — some of our EU customers' data can't leave region. can Redwood run regionally?
06:29 Elena: yes across regions; Dedicated can be region-specific and Private can be fully inside your region. we'll need to discuss network topologies during contract.
06:38 Maya: what's required for a quick POC?
06:41 Elena: sample prompts + dataset, SSO details if you want access, and a short scoping doc for the SE bench. we'll create a pilot plan.
06:48 Raj: great. any gotchas we should watch for?
06:50 Marcus: watch for tokenization surprises (especially CJK), quantization quality regressions, and tail latencies on initial full-context encodes. we'll highlight these in the bench.
07:02 Priya: are there any customers with similar long-context multilingual workloads?
07:05 Elena: yes we've worked with a couple of legal-tech and transcription customers. we'll redact names in references but can share benchmark snapshots.
07:12 Raj: final — competitor question: how do you compare to Anthropic/OpenAI?
07:16 Elena: we focus on inference tooling, deployment flexibility, and cost controls. many customers use open weights for cost reasons; others prefer hosted models. we're agnostic but provide the serving orchestration to make either workable.
07:28 Maya: ok sounds good.
07:30 Elena: recap — Elena will send pricing, SOC2 + KMS docs; Marcus will run the perf plan for 50k context and propose bench parameters; Maya will share eval prompts and dataset snippets; Liam will list residency/regulatory constraints.
07:42 Raj: perfect. thanks everyone.
07:44 Elena: thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the SE deep dive.
07:49 [meeting end]
